ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the BVI FSC Consolidated Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, HM Treasury Consolidated List, and EU Consolidated List. Politically Exposed Persons require enhanced due diligence including source of wealth and source of funds verification; adverse media and negative news screening is mandatory; all CDD documents must be retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs Online System (BVI ROS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in English or in a foreign language using Roman alphabetic characters; where a non-Roman script is used, a certified English transliteration must be delivered with the name reservation application. The legal suffix must be Limited, Ltd., or an approved abbreviation; names must be distinguishable from existing or protected names and must not imply Crown patronage or a regulated activity without the relevant license.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the incorporator or its authorized registered agent may file a written reconsideration request with the BVI Registrar of Corporate Affairs within 14 calendar days, annexing the proposed name, consent letters from any relevant regulator, and evidence of non-conflict. If the reconsideration is refused or no response is given, an appeal may be issued to the BVI High Court within 30 days of the refusal. A reserved name that lapses after 90 days may be re-submitted; no automatic extension is available.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical registered office in the BVI, maintained by a licensed registered agent, is statutorily mandatory. A virtual office address may be used only as an additional correspondence point for non-regulated holding or marketing entities; it cannot replace the statutory registered office. For this foreign manufacturing scope (ISIC 1030 canned tapioca pearl aseptic tubing), no BVI economic substance activity is proposed in the BVI, so physical presence in the BVI is not independently required; however, if a registered office is not duly maintained, the company may be struck off.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low and quantified at approximately 5% per annum; unannounced physical inspections are normally targeted at licensed registered agents, regulated financial institutions, and companies undertaking BVI-relevant activities. A non-resident manufacturing company with a compliant registered agent and no local trading presence is unlikely to be selected for an on-site inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: BVI Business Companies Act, 2004 (as amended), including Part II (Incorporation, ss. 5-12), share capital provisions (ss. 43-46), registered office and registered agent duties (ss. 91-93), and director and officer provisions (ss. 103-110); where the company establishes a UK presence, the Companies Act 2006 (UK), Part 34, and the Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Act 2022 additionally apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry of Corporate Affairs, BVI Financial Services Commission (FSC), Road Town, Tortola, British Virgin Islands; UK filing window: Companies House (UK), Overseas Company Registration unit, Cardiff.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: BVI Form 1 (Application for Incorporation) together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association (M&A) filed electronically via the BVI e-Registry (VITR) portal by a licensed registered agent; UK: Form OS IN01 with certified English translations of the Certificate of Incorporation and M&A.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement exists under the BVI BC Act 2004 (ss. 9, 43); shares may be issued for a nominal par value. Dossier standard: US$50,000 authorized capital, comprising 1,000 ordinary shares of US$0.01 each, fully subscribed and paid by the sole subscriber upon incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the incorporation of the Company, as evidenced by the Certificate of Incorporation dated [●], be and is hereby ratified. RESOLVED FURTHER that the subscriber be allotted 1,000 ordinary shares of US$0.01 par value each; the subscription consideration of US$10.00 being deemed fully paid; and the register of members be updated. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office at [BVI Registered Agent Address, Road Town, Tortola, VG1110, British Virgin Islands] be adopted as the Company's statutory registered office. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Director Name] be appointed sole Director and [Officer Name] be appointed Corporate Secretary, each to hold office until removed. RESOLVED FURTHER that the officers be authorized to open bank accounts, execute agreements, and effect all registrations necessary for UK operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry of Corporate Affairs, BVI FSC - BVI e-Services (VITR portal) via a licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two preferred names in priority order for reservation; the licensed registered agent lodges the name search and government payment; the Registry issues a name approval clearing the proposed name for exclusive use.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of beneficial owner's passport
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, not older than 3 months)
Bank reference letter
Completed BVI AML/KYC questionnaire of the registered agent
Two proposed company names in priority order
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or offensiveness, the agent re-submits the alternative priority name within 2 business days without an additional name fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed BVI Registered Agent (BVI Financial Services Commission licensed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent drafts the M&A in BVI statutory form setting out authorized capital, share classes, and director powers; the subscriber executes the M&A, and each proposed director signs a written consent to act.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (BVI statutory format)
Executed subscriber pages
Consent to act as director for each proposed director
Consent to act as registered agent and registered office by the BVI agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The agent corrects and re-executes the deficient M&A pages, collects a fresh consent signature from the subscriber, and re-schedules the filing to the next e-Registry session.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry of Corporate Affairs, BVI FSC - VITR electronic filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent files BVI Form 1 together with the executed M&A and declaration of compliance through VITR, pays the US$350 government fee, and requests expedited incorporation with same-day issuance.
required_dossiers: BVI Form 1 - Application for Incorporation
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Declaration of compliance under s. 7 of the BC Act
Government filing fee payment voucher (US$350)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On a Registrar query, the agent submits a corrective filing within 14 calendar days using the VITR resubmission workflow; an expedited same-day correction is available for a supplementary fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and statutory corporate kit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry of Corporate Affairs, BVI FSC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation; the registered agent opens the statutory registers (register of members, directors and officers, and charges) and delivers the corporate kit to the client.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar
Share certificates for the issued subscriber shares
Register of members
Register of directors and officers
Registered agent and registered office certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A missing or defective certificate or share certificate is replaced upon surrender of the original, submission of a standard replacement form, and payment of the Registry replacement fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: UK overseas-company registration and transparency filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies House (UK), Overseas Company Registration section; UK Registrar of Overseas Entities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form OS IN01 with certified English translations of the Certificate of Incorporation and M&A, register the UK establishment address and directors/officers, and file the Register of Overseas Entities declaration (ROE01) where a qualifying UK connection exists.
required_dossiers: Form OS IN01 (Notice of Particulars for an Overseas Company)
Certified English translation of the BVI Certificate of Incorporation
Certified English translation of the M&A
Statement of directors, secretary, and UK establishment address
ROE01 application where the company holds a UK asset or qualifying estate
UK filing fee - £44 online or £62 by post
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Companies House rejects a defective application with an error notice; the corrected Form OS IN01 is refiled within 14 days; to avoid penalties on the ROE register, a voluntary late submission with full beneficial-ownership disclosure is made concurrently.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Food Standards Agency (FSA) together with the Local Authority Environmental Health Service (England, Wales and Northern Ireland); Food Standards Scotland in Scotland; Port Health Authority where imported tapioca starch is repacked.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Operator Registration and Low-Acid Canned Food Premises Approval under Regulation (EC) 852/2004 (as retained in the UK) and the Food Safety and Hygiene (England) Regulations 2013, together with a HACCP plan and scheduled-process (12D botulinum microbial lethality) validation for ambient-stable canned boba pearls.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment Agency (England) / Natural Resources Wales / Scottish Environment Protection Agency, plus the relevant UK Water and Sewerage Undertaker for trade effluent consent.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category BR - Basic Regulation: the planned 10 t/day finished-product capacity is below the Schedule 1 (Environmental Permitting Regulations 2016) Part A(2) threshold of 50 t/day, so no LA-IPPC permit is expected; an EIA Screening Opinion is required at planning stage for the new-build canning line, and a full Environmental Statement is not triggered under Annex II thresholds for food factories.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Trade effluent consent (Water Industry Act 1991): pH 6-9, BOD5 <= 300 mg/L, suspended solids <= 350 mg/L, oil and grease <= 100 mg/L, with pre-treatment by screening and pH neutralization; steam boilers of 1-20 MWth meet Medium Combustion Plant Directive limits (NOx <= 300 mg/Nm3, dust <= 50 mg/Nm3); starch sludge and food waste classified as non-hazardous with duty-of-care waste transfer notes; zero ozone-depleting refrigerants and annual leak checks.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Risk Assessment and occupancy certification under the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005; Building Control structural load and means-of-escape completion certificate; HSE notification under RIDDOR 2013; COSHH assessments for caustic cleaning agents, noise-at-work and heat-stress surveys, and workplace-welfare compliance under the Workplace (Health, Safety and Welfare) Regulations 1992.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC); online portal: GOV.UK (gov.uk) via HMRC Online Services / Government Gateway; digital filings through Making Tax Digital (MTD) compatible software.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A BVI Business Company not resident in the UK has no automatic obligation to obtain a UK Corporation Tax Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR) unless it carries on a trade through a UK permanent establishment or UK-source chargeable income arises. For indirect taxes, the BVI BC qualifies as a non-established taxable person (NETP): no turnover threshold applies and VAT registration must be completed before the first UK taxable supply, using HMRC form VAT1 (or the online NETP route) and subsequent MTD-compliant filing. Voluntary VAT registration is available for input VAT recovery where the entity makes taxable supplies in the UK. The entity's ultimate beneficial ownership details must be filed under the UK Register of Overseas Entities (if the BVI BC acquires UK real estate).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (BVI Business Company; non-UK resident entity-level corporation; UK corporation tax charge only arises on trading profits attributable to a UK permanent establishment).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The UK has no check-the-box election. Entity classification follows common-law tests of UK residence and permanent establishment. Available statutory elections include voluntary VAT registration and option to tax on land. Hybrid mismatch rules (Part 6A TIOPA 2010) apply mandatorily and may neutralise deduction/non-inclusion outcomes arising from the tax-exempt BVI classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act 1994, administered by HMRC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: £90,000 VAT registration threshold for UK-established businesses; net nil threshold for non-established taxable persons (BVI BC) requiring registration before the first UK taxable supply; Northern Ireland special rules may treat GB-to-NI flows as imports/exports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory e-invoicing or digital stamping regime. VAT records and returns must be digitised and submitted under Making Tax Digital (MTD) through HMRC-authorised software APIs; customs export declarations are lodged via the Customs Declaration Service (CDS) using electronic API filing with pre-lodge/inventory linking controls.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under VATA 1994 s30 and VAT Notice 703 applies to goods physically exported to a non-UK destination, provided the supplier retains official customs evidence (e.g., CDS export declaration, Bill of Lading, Air Waybill) and the goods leave the UK within 3 months of supply. Canned boba/tapioca pearls sold to offshore buyers are also subject to the place-of-supply rules; services and intangible supplies to B2B customers outside the UK are outside the scope of UK VAT under case law and VAT Notice 741A. Sufficient banking evidence of foreign-currency remittance is required to corroborate export substantiation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CDS Entry Summary / SAD C88 or electronic equivalent)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill endorsed to the UK exporter
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the export declaration
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT MT103 evidencing foreign currency payment receipt
UK food-export documentary evidence (health certificates or exporter registration under FSA/Defra) for canned food products
Trader's records of movement and dispatch (delivery notes, carrier contracts) as supplementary proof under VAT Notice 703
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: HMRC may issue assessments for up to 4 years (6 years for careless inaccuracies, 20 years for deliberate VAT evasion) retrospectively clawing back zero-rating where export evidence is deficient. Penalties range from 30% (careless) to 100% (deliberate concealment) of the tax under FA 2007 Schedule 24 and VATA 1994 s72, together with late-payment interest, naming-and-shaming publication, director disqualification, and criminal prosecution for fraudulent evasion; exporters must retain prescribed evidence for the statutory period or face full reversal of VAT zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (monetary, payments and foreign-exchange market infrastructure) and HM Treasury (licensing and sanctions) via the Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018; no dedicated foreign-exchange administration exists because the Exchange Control Act 1947 was repealed in 1979, leaving full liberalisation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The United Kingdom has accepted Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement (since 15 February 1961), guaranteeing full convertibility on both current and capital account without exchange controls, prior approval or payment-transfer restrictions. Profit remittance, dividends, branch remittances and loan repayments are freely repatriable for the BVI Business Company; practical hurdles are limited to bank-level AML/KYC, FATCA/CRS certification, OFSI sanctions screening and the absence of UK withholding tax on dividends or arm's length interest. Royalties and certain contingent technical-service fees may attract 20% UK withholding subject to double-tax-treaty relief, and UK-sourced trading profits of the UK manufacturing branch remain within UK corporation tax.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, repatriation or conversion requirements apply. Since October 1979 the UK has had zero mandatory timelines for bringing export receipts onshore and zero mandatory conversion ratios; receipts may be retained in any currency in any approved or unapproved account without central-bank notification, subject only to HMRC transfer-pricing documentation, the UK CFC rules and any UN/OFSI sanctions blocking specific counterparties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-currency International Operations Account (Operational with Capital Escrow overlay via HSBC International Banking Centre)
Commercial Operational Account with Import/Export Trade Finance module

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for operational GBP/EUR/USD payment accounts, FX execution and treasury float, via FCA-regulated e-money institutions (for example Wise, Revolut Business, Airwallex UK, Ebury, Currencycloud and Starling-based programmes) that onboard BVI Business Companies remotely within 5-10 business days using eID&V and EDD. Legal constraints: EMIs under the Electronic Money Regulations 2011 and Payment Services Regulations 2017 cannot hold deposit/capital escrow balances, do not provide lending or banker's acceptance facilities, must safeguard client funds in tier-1 UK banks, and each institution applies its own OFSI sanctions screening and sectoral exclusions; therefore the EMIs are a corridor-level solution, not the escrow/capital-raise solution, and the ultimate high-value settlement rail remains CHAPS/SWIFT at tier-1 clearing banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement for directors to appear physically at a UK branch; FCA Finalised Guidance FG17/6 explicitly permits electronic identity verification and video interviews for remote onboarding, and the Money Laundering Regulations 2017 impose an outcome-based customer due diligence obligation rather than an in-person rule. In practice tier-1 clearing banks demand a recorded video interview with all directors/shareholders of the BVI BC, a UK-nexus referral, or a sponsoring relationship for non-resident structures; fully remote opening without any physical attendance is realistically achievable primarily through FCA-regulated EMIs and fintech banks, with tier-1 banks still requiring a London-based signatory or account-executive meeting at the Medium/Low tiers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: BVI legal-person opacity: no UK entity registration, nominee shareholding and beneficial ownership filed only with the BVI government
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles, Certificate of Good Standing from the BVI Financial Services Commission; full Register of Directors and Register of Members; UBO declaration covering every natural person above 25% (with economic interest above 10% shown as good practice); licensed BVI registered-agent letter confirming independence of nominee arrangements; corporate chart of the entire VG_BC group.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: BVI Economic Substance (Companies and Limited Partnerships) Act 2018 screening: a BVI manufacturing/trading company must demonstrate it is not claiming an inconsistent substance exemption
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of BVI NS1/ES e-filing confirming exempt/holding or reduced substance status; management accounts showing the business is run from the UK entity; description of UK assets, employees and office; intercompany services agreements; Corporate Tax provision certificate showing tax-transparent BVI status under the Stage 3 UK tax assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: OFSI/UN/EU/OFAC sanctions and PEP exposure from non-resident shareholders, supply chains or the boba trade counterparties (added scrutiny on Chinese-origin tapioca starch and shipping lanes)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed sanctions and PEP screening matrix with full name/BIC/date-of-birth data; copies of directors' passports and utility proofs; import/export contracts with end-user and non-dual-use declarations confirming tapioca pearls as foodstuff (NAICS 311999); certificates of origin; shipping-party vessel and airway OFAC checks; a written OFSI compliance note and refusal-to-deal log.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds/wealth of the capital injection and stored-value transaction patterns from canned-boba inventory sales
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised source-of-wealth and source-of-funds letters; 12-month shareholder bank statements; capital subscription wire evidence; signed supply/purchase/sales contracts; inventory aging and valuation schedule for canned/aseptic tapioca pearls; audited or management-prepared IFRS financial statements; tax payment references to HMRC CT/VAT and BVI income tax exemption.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FATCA/CRS classification mismatch or ambiguous UK tax residency status of the non-UK parent (unverified GIIN and unchecked CRS entity type)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRS self-certification selecting the correct entity type and tax-residency jurisdiction (BVI or GB per Stage 3); GIIN registration evidence where required; IRS Form W-8BEN-E with entity classification; UK HMRC tax-district confirmation or negative-residence opinion; BVI tax exemption certificate; reconciliation letter explaining the UK tax transparency file produced in Stages 1-3.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant route: BVI parent initiates a SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank cover) to the UK receiving bank, stating 'shareholder capital contribution / equity injection' as the reason-for-payment; the UK bank credits the Operational Account via the CHAPS net settlement for value-date availability (or Faster Payments if below £1,000,000); the inbound credit is screened against the OFSI consolidated list, OFAC and EU sanctions, then against the bank's own CRS/FATCA records. Supporting documents retained: board resolution approving the capital call, share subscription agreement, updated Register of Members and capital-contribution allocation ledger. The UK has no exchange-control approval, no capital import duty and no mandatory declaration to the Bank of England, but the remitter and recipient must preserve evidence of the corporate purpose to rebut any money-laundering presumption.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for tapioca-pearl raw materials and finished-goods trade use (a) SWIFT MT103 customer transfers for international TT/wire payments; (b) Commercial Letters of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700/MT720/MT707 under UCP600, with presentation of commercial invoice, bill of lading/airway bill, certificate of origin and health/phyto certificates, settled by MT202 cover through CHAPS or correspondent accounts; (c) CHAPS for high-value same-day GBP payments; (d) Faster Payments/Bacs for low-value UK domestic suppliers; and (e) CLS (Continuous Linked Settlement) to eliminate FX settlement risk on the GBP/EUR/USD legs. All outflows are mapped against HMRC VAT/CT filings and the BVI intercompany ledger, and must retain UK Port Health Authority clearance certificates for food imports because tapioca starch is a controlled foodstuff under the Official Controls Regulations 2019.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (including window forwards and spot-deferred contracts) traded under an ISDA Master Agreement with UK banks or FCA-regulated investment firms, tenors from 1 month to 24 months for GBP/USD, GBP/EUR, GBP/CNY and GBP/THB; subject to UK EMIR reporting and margining rules when above the clearing threshold.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or insufficiently liquid currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, VND, IDR, MYR) where onshore deliverability is barred or costly; legally permissible for a BVI BC via UK banks that trade offshore NDFs without triggering local regulatory licensing.

Cross-currency swaps and FX swaps to hedge long-term capital-injection mismatch, trade receivables/payables and intercompany loan re-denomination; permitted for UK-resident and non-resident counterparties under UK MiFIR/MiFID II with appropriate appropriateness assessments.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% main rate for profits exceeding £250,000; 19% Small Profits Rate for profits up to £50,000; marginal relief (taper) between £50,001 and £250,000 — Finance Act 2021, CTA 2010 ss.18A–18DX, applicable for FY2024 (1 April 2024 – 31 March 2025). A BVI Business Company is not itself subject to BVI corporate income tax (0% BVI rate), but once UK tax resident (central management and control in the UK) or operating through a UK permanent establishment (PE), UK Corporation Tax applies at 19%–25% on attributable profits.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Patent Box: effective 10% rate on qualifying IP profits derived from patented boba processing or aseptic packaging inventions (CTA 2010 Part 8A); Full Expensing: 100% first-year allowance on qualifying plant and machinery acquired before 31 March 2026 (CAA 2001 s.52A); 50% first-year allowance on special-rate assets; Annual Investment Allowance: £1 million per annum; R&D Expenditure Credit (RDEC): 20% taxable credit for large and SME companies (CTA 2009 Part 13); Enhanced SME R&D relief: 86% additional deduction plus 12.5% payable credit for loss-making SMEs; Investment Zone and Freeport enhanced capital allowance regimes for qualifying manufacturing sites.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite) carry-forward of trading losses under CTA 2010 s.45; pre-2017 losses carry forward against total future trading profits, post-2017 losses are subject to the £5 million annual offset cap beyond which only 50% of the remaining chargeable profits may be relieved (CTA 2010 ss.188A–188DD). UK capital losses carry forward indefinitely against chargeable gains only.
